newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end flat, seen staying lacklustre.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end flat, seen staying lacklustre.

text.p: Singapore shares ended Tuesday little changed as investors stayed sidelined. Dealers said the market was likely to remain lacklustre in the near term.
"Investors are not inspired and I can't see anything in the market that's going to get it moving," said a dealer with a local brokerage.
The Straits Times Industrials Index reversed from a slightly negative region to end at 2,061.22, up by 0.32 point. Market volume was 153.4 million shares with 241 losers and 114 gainers.
"There is selling, but it doesn't seem to be part of a major sell programme," another dealer said.

Dealers said the day's only interest came from DBS Land, whcih revealed plans to raise Singapore $427 million (US$298.6 million) through a share placement to finance its purchase of a stake in healthcare group Parkway Holdings.
DBS Land took 19 percent of Parkway in May and said it would like more. Parkway shares rose on DBS Land's placement news to end the day up S0.10 at S$7.00. DBS Land suspended its trade.

Debut listing Benefun International provided dealers with the only other bright spot on an otherwise dull horizon, hitting a high of Hong Kong $1.70 against its HK$1.15 offer price before ending the day at HK$1.44.
